Agentic AI is moving quickly from impressive demos to real production systems. But reliable agents require more than strong models and clever prompts and tools.
🧰 They need a harness. Harness Engineering is hottest 🌶️ topic of the 2026.

⚽️ FIFA World Cup Semi Final happening on the day so we will wrap up the main event before 8 PM and   🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 England are playing and we are live streaming the semi final from the event venue.
🎫 Please bring a valid photo ID with you for venue entry as it's mandatory requirement.
A production agent harness is the engineering layer around the model: runtime, tools, memory, identity, permissions, security boundaries, evaluations, observability, debugging, deployment workflows and feedback loops. It is the difference between an agent that works in a demo and an agent that can safely operate in the real world.
Join London Agentic AI hosted by Amazon for a deep technical evening on Harness Engineering: the practical discipline of building, deploying, testing and operating production-ready AI agents.
This event will explore how agent builders design the full operating environment required for reliable agentic systems.

What We’ll Cover
What Harness Engineering means and why it matters now

How production agents differ from prototypes

Agent runtime, tool access, memory and identity patterns

Secure execution, sandboxing and enterprise system integration

Evaluation, tracing, observability and debugging for agents

Real-world lessons from building and operating agent harnesses

Speakers and Talks
🎙️ Talk 1: Agents FC: Harness Your Agents Into a Winning Team
Speaker:  Anisha Malde : Senior Developer Advocate at Amazon
Abstract: Multi-agent orchestration is powerful, but without a defined harness around it, it's a black box. Agents route dynamically, hand off silently, and hallucinate. Harness engineering is about designing the scaffolding around your agents: the environments they work in, how context gets delivered, how outputs get verified, how plans get captured, how the agents coordinate, and where & when humans can intervene.

What if you could organise & coach your agents like a World Cup football team? "Agents FC" is our analogy for harness engineering and orchestration as a football team. Each agent role maps to a tested orchestration pattern: the Captain coordinates routing, the Playmaker retrieves context, the Striker delivers the output, the Defenders run mid-flight verification, and the Goalkeeper catches failures at the output boundary before they escape. And then there's the harness: how they pass the ball between each other, what tools each one carries on the pitch, how the team learns from a missed shot, and how every move gets logged so you, as the manager, can change formation mid-task to restructure the orchestration, make substitutions when a strategy isn't working, or call a "half-time team talk" to review progress.
🎙️Talk 2 : Pydantic AI Harness Engineering 

Speaker: Samuel Colvin:  CEO of Pydantic AI
Abstract: Coming soon

🎙️ Talk 3 : Omnigent: A meta-harness for AI Agents

Speaker: Sultan Al Awar : Solutions Architect at Databricks
Abstract: Coding agents are everywhere, but enterprises face fragmented tooling, security risk, and hard choices of models and harnesses. This talk introduces Omnigent, a Databricks open source meta-harness that enables agent composition, enforces contextual policies that keep security and cost in control, and supports real-time human collaboration across live agent sessions. 

Bio: Solutions Architect at Databricks, working with Digital Natives Businesses in energy, health-tech and insurance industries.

Rare Build Hackathon
Hosted by Rare Founders × Mollie
One day. One room. 150 builders. Don't just build a product - build a business.
📅 11 July 2026 · 📍 The Ministry, London Bridge · 🕘 9:00 AM - 10:00 PM
What this is
A full-day, invite-only hackathon hosted by Rare Founders and Mollie. 150 of London's sharpest builders, designers, operators, and marketers in one room, forming teams on the spot, and shipping a real business by the end of the day.
This isn't a typical hackathon. We're not asking you to build a demo. We're asking you to build something people will actually buy.
You come up with the idea. You research it. You talk to real customers. You build it. You package it. You sell it.
By 7 PM, you'll pitch a product, a price, and proof someone wants it.
The challenge
Every team goes through the full startup loop in a single day:
Form the team → find your co-builders during the morning matchmaking.
Find the idea → no themes, no categories. You decide what's worth building.
Talk to real customers → leave the venue. Walk to the nearest coffee shop, office, high street, or co-working space. Talk to as many people as you can. Real validation, real conversations, real feedback. Bring the evidence back.
Build the product → engineers and designers build and package the solution while commercial team members validate, position, and sell.
Package it → name it, price it, position it, design the landing page, write the pitch.
Sell it → letters of intent, waitlist signups, pre-orders, paying customers. With Mollie's payment integration available on the day, you can actually take real money from real customers in real time. We'll count every form of validation. The strongest evidence wins.
Pitch it → defend your business on stage in front of judges who've built and backed real companies.
Thinking outside the box is the whole point. We know not every idea can generate revenue in a single day. What we want to see is teams doing everything they possibly can to prove the value. The teams that find the most creative ways to validate will stand out.
One rule: no gaming the system. Letters of intent must come from your actual target audience. Paying customers must be real. We're not interested in mates filling out forms. We're interested in evidence that strangers want what you've built.
Why this needs a full team
This format is impossible without all three disciplines on the team. That's not marketing copy. It's how the day actually works.
Technical → builds the product.
Design → packages it, names it, makes it feel real.
Commercial  Sales  Marketing → does the customer research, runs the outreach, secures the validation, writes the pitch, closes the sales.
If you've been on the commercial side wondering whether a hackathon is for you, this one is built around you. While the engineers and designers build, you're the one out talking to customers, testing positioning, securing the LOIs, and closing the sales. The team can't win without you.
Format
150 attendees, max. Applications reviewed. Not everyone gets in.

Teams form on the day. Matchmaking from 9:30. You leave the morning with a team or you don't build.

Minimum 2 per team, maximum 4. Ideal mix: one technical, one design, one commercial.

Open brief. Build whatever you want, for whoever you want.

You can leave the venue. Talking to real customers is encouraged. Bring the evidence back.

Mollie payment integration available for teams that want to take real payments on the day.

Submissions close at 7:00 PM. All teams submit. Judges review and the top 10 are announced.

Top 10 pitch on the main stage. 3-5 minutes each, including Q&A from the judges.

Every team must be ready to pitch. Even if you don't make the top 10, build pitch prep into your day. Plan for it.

Each business is judged individually. No artificial categories. The strongest businesses win.

Everything provided. Food, drinks, Wi-Fi, infrastructure credits, AI access, database templates, payment integration. Show up with a laptop.

How you'll be judged
Three judges. Three lenses. One winner.
Business viability - Is this a real business? Is there a market? Did you prove it? Caroline Frankum - Former CEO of Kantar, the world's largest user research company.
Investability - Would I put money into this team and this idea? David Gilgur - Partner at Blue Lake VC and Ken Thomas - Principal at BackFuture VC
Technical execution - Did you actually build something? Is it solid? Could it scale? Fergus McKenzie-Wilson - CTO and Co-Founder at 60x.
Each judge weights what matters most for their lens, and we'll factor in what kind of business you've built when deciding how the criteria apply. A consumer product and a B2B SaaS prove value in different ways.
Mentors will be on the floor throughout the day to help teams unblock, sharpen their pitch, and answer questions across technical, design, and commercial challenges. Use them.

10:00 PM Doors close

If you don't make the top 10, you stay, you watch, you drink, you network. The day doesn't end at 7.
Why apply
You'll meet people you'd never normally meet. Ten hours, shoulder-to-shoulder, with people you didn't know at 9 AM.

You'll build a real business in a day. Not a demo, not a deck. A product with customers attached.

You'll pitch in front of judges who matter. Even if you don't make the top 10, the right person seeing your work is worth the day.

You'll learn what it actually takes to ship. Most people never get this compressed.

You'll walk out with a network, not a tote bag. Past Rare Founders teams have gone on to raise, co-found, and hire from each other.

You'll have fun. Free food, free drinks, free infrastructure, and 150 people who chose to spend their day building.

Apply

42 hours. 500 builders. $65K in prizes, plus $1.5M in Mubit credits.
Night Shift is an overnight hackathon in London, built around Mubit. Route your LLM calls through Mubit with one base URL change, then turn your corrections into model updates for the recurring tasks your product runs.
Every LLM call should count towards owning your intelligence layer. This weekend you build the proof.
It's also the night the UK clocks go back, so you get an extra hour :D
Prizes: $65K
One of the largest AI hackathon prize pools London has seen.
1st place: $15,000 cash

2nd place: $10,000 cash

3rd place: $5,000 cash

$35,000 in credits: OpenAI API credits and other AI credits

On top of the prize pool: $1.5M in Mubit credits for accepted hackers.
Early bird: the first 50 accepted hackers get $50 in OpenAI API credits at check-in.
What you'll build
Mubit sits between your application and its model calls. It generates lightweight model updates from your calls and feedback, so the calls you already make become task-adapted open models. The base models stay fixed, and updates are built for fast refresh as your workload changes.
The brief: build a product that routes its LLM calls through Mubit and turns your corrections into model updates for a recurring task.
Pick a track:
Recurring tasks. Choose a task your product runs again and again: extraction, triage, support replies, review, routing. Show your corrections becoming model updates.

Own your intelligence layer. Take a workload you'd normally send to a closed model and move it onto a task-adapted open model. Show quality, cost and latency side by side.

Fast refresh. Build for a workload that keeps changing: new data, new customers, new domains. Show your model updates keeping pace.

The top 3 prizes are judged across all tracks.
Judging
Four criteria, weighted equally:
Use of Mubit. Show a correction turning into a model update in your demo.

Usefulness. A real recurring task someone would want handled.

Technical execution. It works, and it holds up under questions.

Demo. Clear, live, and under the time limit.

Who should apply
Software engineers, AI engineers, founders, designers and students who ship. Students are welcome, as long as you're 18+. If you can make an API call, you can use Mubit. You don't need ML experience, and you don't need a team to apply. Come solo and find a team at kickoff.
How to apply
Apply on this page. It takes about three minutes.

We review on a rolling basis. Applications close Sunday 18 October. Accepted hackers get early access to Mubit and API keys by email before the event.

Good to know
Where: Central London. The exact venue is shared with accepted hackers.

Teams: 1 to 4 people. Solo hackers welcome.

Eligibility: 18+, in person only. At least one team member must be at Sunday's demos to win.

Food: all meals, snacks and caffeine are covered for all 42 hours.

Sleep: bring a sleeping bag or pillow if you plan to stay overnight. You can also go home and come back.

Bring: laptop, charger, photo ID for check-in, toiletries.

Travel: we can't reimburse travel.

Rules: all project code is written during the event. Open-source libraries and your own tooling are fine. Every project must route its LLM calls through Mubit.

Photos and video: if you're accepted and attend, you agree that we can photograph and film you at the event and post it on Mubit's social channels and elsewhere on social media.

Code of conduct: be kind and respectful to everyone. Harassment, discrimination or abusive behaviour of any kind isn't tolerated, and anyone who breaks this may be asked to leave.

FAQ
How much does it cost?
Nothing. Night Shift is free.
Do I need to know how to fine-tune models?
No. Mubit runs adapter fine-tuning for you, automatically. All you change is one base URL.
Do I have to stay overnight?
No. The venue stays open the whole time, so stay as long as you like.
Can I start building before Friday?
Bring ideas and research. Code starts at kickoff.
Who owns what I build?
You do.
When will I hear back?
We review on a rolling basis, so apply early. Everyone hears back by Tuesday 20 October.
Hosts
Hosted by the Mubit team. Judges will be announced later.
